Main.id: Energy policy of the United States - Wikipedia#115

Main.id: Energy policy of the United States - Wikipedia#127

Main.id: Energy policy of the United States - Wikipedia#129

Main.id: Energy policy of the United States - Wikipedia#161

Main.id: Energy policy of the United States - Wikipedia#165

Main.id: Energy policy of the United States - Wikipedia#167
Main.sentence: The ___E:Energy Policy Act of 2005 U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Energy_Policy_Act_of_2005)___ (EPAct) expanded federal authority to regulate power transmission.

Main.id: Energy policy of the United States - Wikipedia#168
Main.sentence: EPAct gave FERC significant new responsibilities, including enforcement of electric transmission reliability standards and the establishment of rate incentives to encourage investment in electricity transmission.

Main.id: Energy policy of the United States - Wikipedia#170

Main.sentence: For example, some regulators in Maine refused to address congestion problems because the congestion protects Maine rates.

Main.id: Energy policy of the United States - Wikipedia#175

Main.id: Energy policy of the United States - Wikipedia#176

Main.id: Energy policy of the United States - Wikipedia#177
Main.sentence: The Order was challenged in court by the state public utility commissions via the ___E:National Association of Regulatory Utility Commissioners (NARUC) U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Association_of_Regulatory_Utility_Commissioners)___ , the ___E:American Public Power Association U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Public_Power_Association)___ , and others who claimed that FERC overstepped its jurisdiction by regulating how local electric distribution and behind-the-meter facilities are administered, i.e., by not providing an opt-out of wholesale market access for energy storage facilities located at the distribution level or behind-the-meter.

Main.id: Energy policy of the United States - Wikipedia#178
Main.sentence: The ___E:D.C. Circuit Court U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Court_of_Appeals_for_the_District_of_Columbia_Circuit)___ issued an order in July 2020 that upheld Order 841 and dismissed the petitioners' complaints.

Main.id: Energy policy of the United States - Wikipedia#179
Main.sentence: FERC issued Order 2222 on September 17, 2020, enabling ___E:distributed energy resources U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Distributed_generation)___ such as batteries and ___E:demand response U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Demand_response)___ to participate in regional wholesale electricity markets.

Main.id: Energy policy of the United States - Wikipedia#180
Main.sentence: Market operators submitted initial compliance plans by early 2022.  The Supreme Court had ruled in 2016 in FERC v. Electric Power Supply Ass'n that the agency had the authority to regulate ___E:demand response U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Demand_response)___ transactions.

Main.id: Energy policy of the United States - Wikipedia#181
Main.sentence: $11 billion of the $73 billion from the ___E:Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Infrastructure_Investment_and_Jobs_Act)___ will be invested in the ___E:electrical grid U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electrical_grid)___ 's adjustment to ___E:renewable energy U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Renewable_energy)___ , with some of the money going to new loans for ___E:electric power transmission U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electric_power_transmission)___ lines and required studies for future transmission needs.

Main.id: Energy policy of the United States - Wikipedia#182
Main.sentence: On October 24, 2023, the administration announced that the first $3.46 billion in grants from the Act's $11 billion grid rebuilding authorization would go to 58 projects in 44 states. 16 projects are categorized as improving grid resilience, 34 are categorized as building ___E:smart grids U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smart_grid)___ , and eight are categorized as pursuing grid innovation.

Main.id: Energy policy of the United States - Wikipedia#184

Main.id: Energy policy of the United States - Wikipedia#185

Main.id: Energy policy of the United States - Wikipedia#186

Main.id: Energy policy of the United States - Wikipedia#187

Main.id: Energy policy of the United States - Wikipedia#189

Main.id: Energy policy of the United States - Wikipedia#190
Main.sentence: The following April 25, the DOE announced the TFP selection of the 2-gigawatt Southwest Intertie Project North, which effectively extends the ___E:One Nevada Transmission Line U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/One_Nevada_Transmission_Line)___ northward to Idaho.

Main.id: Energy policy of the United States - Wikipedia#191
Main.sentence: The next October, the DOE announced that four projects, the 1.2-gigawatt Aroostook Project in Maine, 1.9-gigawatt Cimarron Link in Oklahoma, 3-gigawatt Southern Spirit between Texas and Mississippi, and 1-gigawatt Southline in New Mexico, were being awarded a total of $1.5 billion under the TFP; the DOE also released its first ever National Transmission Planning Study to follow up on the Needs Study, forecasting a needed national transmission capacity increase of 2.4 to 3.5 times the 2020 level by 2050 to keep costs low and facilitate the energy transmission, with estimated cost savings ranging from $270 billion to $490 billion.

Main.id: Energy policy of the United States - Wikipedia#192
Main.sentence: The Inflation Reduction Act of the Biden administration has fast-tracked transmission projects by helping purchase $30 billion in wholesale electric transmission contracts, as well as by publishing a national transmission needs report, which had been expanded in scope by the ___E:Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Infrastructure_Investment_and_Jobs_Act)___ .

Main.id: Energy policy of the United States - Wikipedia#195
Main.sentence: On July 28, 2023, the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission approved Order No. 2023, which regulates the interconnection process that ties renewables projects into the large-scale grid. Main.id: Energy policy of the United States - Wikipedia#196
